Priya (Customer): Hey team — starting ~2026-03-16 09:12 UTC our service behind acme-dedicated (tenant acme-co) started getting a wave of 429s and some high tail latency. Only started after we switched plans for a subset of users last night. Can someone take a look? We're seeing failures in production.

Sam (Support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the X-RateLimit headers and a short sample of the request ids/trace ids you saw? Also which pool (quiet/standard) is this using?

Priya (Customer): Pool: reserved-acme-standard. Example headers from one failed call:
```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1678901234
X-RateLimit-Unit: minute
x-request-id: rq_01Habc123
```
Trace id: trace-9a7c

Alan (Oncall Ops): Hmm X-RateLimit-Unit: minute stands out. If that tenant was supposed to be per-token units but got mapped as per-minute the rate math could be off (60x discrepancy). Can you confirm the plan id that was migrated?

Priya (Customer): Plan id: legacy-pro-minute -> migrated-to: pro-default. We thought migration would preserve token-based units.

Ingrid (Eng-SRE): I'm looking at the migration job logs now. Quick check query I ran against config_db:
```
SELECT tenant_id, plan_id, rate_unit, rate_multiplier, created_at
FROM tenant_rate_profiles
WHERE tenant_id = 'acme-co';
```
Result: tenant_id=acme-co, plan_id=migrated-pro, rate_unit='minute', rate_multiplier='1'

Ingrid (Eng-SRE): That explains it — the migration preserved the 'minute' unit and we interpret that as 100 calls/minute, but our serving runtime expects per-token units for this plan. So per-tenant limit effectively much lower than intended.

Sam (Support): Thanks. Could this be a legacy-plan-lookup mapping bug where the billing -> serving mapping doesn't convert minutes->tokens (or apply multiplier)?

Alan (Oncall Ops): Likely. I'll run a quick count of affected tenants to gauge blast radius:
```
SELECT count(*) FROM tenant_rate_profiles
WHERE plan_id LIKE 'legacy-%' AND rate_unit IN ('minute','hour');
```
Result: 12 tenants affected (small number).

Ingrid (Eng-SRE): Proposed immediate mitigation: backfill tenant_rate_profiles.rate_unit = 'token' and set rate_multiplier = rate_multiplier * avg_tokens_per_minute_estimate for migrated tenants, then force config reload on serving proxies for those tenant_ids. Example SQL:
```
UPDATE tenant_rate_profiles
SET rate_unit='token', rate_multiplier = rate_multiplier * 500
WHERE tenant_id = 'acme-co' AND rate_unit='minute';
```
(500 tokens/minute is conservative estimate; we can tailor per-customer later.)

Alan (Oncall Ops): I'll prepare a targeted DB update and a 1-host config reload to test.

deploy-bot: Scheduled config reload: reload-config job queued for service=redwood-serving-proxy, target=reserved-acme-standard, tenant_filter=acme-co

Sam (Support): Priya — we'll do this as a limited fix and monitor. Do you have a short window to accept occasional blips while we apply the change?

Priya (Customer): Yes please patch now. We're getting 5-10% error rate right now, blocking checkout flows.

Alan (Oncall Ops): Running update now (must be run with safety flag):
```
-- dry-run first
BEGIN;
UPDATE tenant_rate_profiles
SET rate_unit='token', rate_multiplier = rate_multiplier * 600
WHERE tenant_id='acme-co' AND rate_unit='minute';
-- verify
SELECT tenant_id, rate_unit, rate_multiplier FROM tenant_rate_profiles WHERE tenant_id='acme-co';
COMMIT;
```

Ingrid (Eng-SRE): After dry-run verified, applied commit and restarted one proxy (canary). Observability: error rate dropped from 9% -> 1.2% on canary host, tail latency improved.

deploy-bot: reload-config job completed for host=proxy-09, status=success

Sam (Support): Rolling the change to remaining hosts now.

Priya (Customer): I'm seeing 429s drop in dashboards, thank you. Can you follow up with a permanent fix? This migration should never change the unit semantics.

Ingrid (Eng-SRE): Action items:
- Hotfix backfill applied to affected tenants (12) — completed for 6 so far, running for remaining 6 (in progress).
- Create a migration validation that rejects plan_migration if unit conversion is ambiguous.
- Add alerting rule: if tenant_rate_profiles.rate_unit != expected_unit_for_plan then warn in console and page.
- Update docs for plan schema and add unit tests in billing->serving mapper.

Alan (Oncall Ops): I'll open a short-lived runbook for support to triage this if it recurs and include the one-liner SQL to backfill.

Sam (Support): Noted. Priya — can you confirm traffic looks nominal in the next 30m and we can close the thread?

Priya (Customer): Confirmed — 30m window looks good, error budget recovered. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :heart:

Ingrid (Eng-SRE): Postmortem will include root cause: plan migration left legacy 'minute' unit untouched; codepath expected 'token' unit for pro plans. We'll propose a schema migration and an automated conversion table.

Alan (Oncall Ops): Follow-up tech tasks tracked in ENG-INF-4212. I'll assign owners and timelines.

Sam (Support): Closing loop here — will reopen if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:
